pages.title: External Dependency Intelligence - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: Independent knowledge about the third-party services your product depends on.

pages.title: Dependency Monitoring - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: Continuous third-party observation with deterministic fault confirmation.

pages.title: Incident Attribution - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: Determining whether an incident originated inside your stack or with a vendor.

pages.title: SLA Evidence - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: Timestamped, checksummed records of vendor behavior for credit conversations.

pages.title: Vendor Reliability - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: How consistently a third-party service meets its expected behavior over time.

pages.title: Dependency Telemetry - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: The raw observations behind every reliability claim: checks, outcomes, timestamps.

pages.title: Infrastructure Evidence - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: Verifiable records of how infrastructure behaved during a window.

pages.title: External Dependency Fault Report - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: The artifact that attributes a failure window to a specific dependency.

pages.title: Independent Measurement - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: A record produced by an observer with no stake in the outcome, from its own requests.

pages.title: Quorum Detection - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: Confirming a dependency incident only when independent observation points agree.

pages.title: Transport Error - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: A failure below HTTP: the request never produced a complete response.

pages.title: Vendor-Reported Status - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: What a provider says about itself - one record among several, not the ground truth.

pages.title: Partial Outage - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: A dependency failing for some traffic, regions, routes or models - not all of them.

pages.title: Availability - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: The share of scheduled observations that received the expected response, per stated window.

pages.title: Latency - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: Time from probe dispatch to complete response - the leading indicator of degradation.

pages.title: Observation density - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: Observations that exist, against observations the schedule implies.

pages.title: Telemetry integrity - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: Whether a record can be trusted to be complete, correctly labelled and auditable.

pages.title: Dependency blast radius - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: The set of your functionality that fails when one external dependency does.

pages.title: Failure domain - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: The set of components that fail together, and therefore must be reasoned about together.

pages.title: Control plane - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: The part of a system that decides what should happen.

pages.title: Data plane - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: The part of a system that carries the workload.

pages.title: External trust boundary - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: The line where your controls stop and a third party’s begin.

pages.title: AI API dependency - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: A model reached over the network - a dependency whose payload you only partly control.

pages.title: Model routing - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: The provider-side decision about what actually serves your request.

pages.title: Observability blind spot - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: A failure mode your instrumentation is structurally unable to report.

pages.title: Explicit deny - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: A policy statement with Effect Deny that overrides every Allow it matches.

pages.title: Implicit deny - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: The default refusal a request receives when nothing in scope explicitly allows it.

pages.title: Identity-based policy - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: A policy attached to an IAM principal that states what that principal may do.

pages.title: Resource-based policy - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: A policy attached to a resource that states who may act on it.

pages.title: Permissions boundary - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: A policy that caps the maximum permissions an IAM principal can be granted.

pages.title: Non-human identity - Definition | RELIASTRA
pages.description: A principal that is a workload rather than a person: service roles, pipelines, agents.
